doc.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15

title: Repertoire, a photograph of Chris, and his reputation
summary: Edna cannot recall slow blues numbers, describes the hunt for a picture of Chris held by his nieces Pearl and Lena, and ranks him among the city's best.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Hunting for old band photographs and scrapbooks

blocks.x: And, um, did they ever play, um, did they ever play any, what you might call, real lowdown numbers, you know, where, um, they played real quiet?
Tiger Ray. Like that.
Well, no, I wasn't thinking so much like they had this, um, you know, real sort of slow blues, but they played real quiet and, um, sort of, you know, lowdown, you might say.
Oh yeah, they played all kinds, but I can't, now.
Blank now. Mine's blank. Mm-hmm.
All kinds of, all kinds of music, all kinds.
Let me ask you this, did you ever find a, did you ever see a picture of Chris Kelly?
Yes, I had someone. Ah. Yes.
What did, uh, what did, what did, what did you describe it to him?
Just like I told you. Looked just like him, but he had, he had, he had, he used to wear a little dog, a little black Dewey Bay. Yeah. Should be a Dewey Bay hat.
Yeah.
Always, anytime you saw him, he had that cigar in his mouth, on one side of his mouth. Yeah. Talk with him, and there, at a red spot right here. Yeah.

But what I was talking about more was the picture, because I've heard that there's a picture, that somebody said they'd seen a picture of him when he was wearing his army uniform, and I was wondering if this is the picture you're talking about.
Well, that might be, well, he, no, no, he wasn't wearing an army uniform. He had a picture somewhere in his army uniform, because he had went to the army.
But the one you remember is not that?
No. The one I remember was just a plain picture. His niece had, and his niece died, I don't remember.
His niece died? Yeah.

She was the one who lived on St. Anne and Quillerie? No, not that one, but there was two sisters of them. One was named Pearl, and one was named Lena. The one St. Anne and Quillerie was named Lena, and the one across the river was named Pearl. She was the one who had a picture.
Yeah. Is Lena still alive? Lena Porter? Yeah, I think she is. Well, maybe she had it.
No, she don't. I had that.
Oh, you had it. Pearl had it. But Pearl didn't give it to her? No. What about Pearl's children? She don't have it.
She didn't have it.
She was a nice to find out for her.
He was a great man, though. They resisted in this town. Yes, he was. He was the best. Him. Kid Ran A. Good. Sam Morgan, remember that?

Well, I don't, I won't, you know, it's all before my time. I don't, it was done. Yeah, all that's before your time. Yeah, so I mean, that's why, you know, that's why people would, we need to ask people like you, really, because, you know, there's not too many people around now that can remember those times.
That's about all I know now.
